description: The third state, kept separate on purpose (S64): this worker was running when the daemon died or shut down, and the next daemon's recovery sweep wrote the row — the process that owned the work is gone, so nobody knows what it half-did, and NOTHING re-fires it (the registry is code, and a silently restarted ten-minute parse is a loop nobody agreed to). The row is the invitation to retry deliberately from the app; `error` says who said no — the daemon by dying, not the work by refusing (that is asyncworker.failed).

payload.error: daemon stopped before the worker finished
